title: LabBook: Harnessing Experimental History for Efficient LLM-Driven Discovery
abstract: arXiv:2610.00675v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Evolutionary approaches to LLM-driven discovery often generate new programs from a small set of selected ancestors. This keeps contexts manageable but can omit useful evidence from other experiments, whereas including the full experimental history produces long, redundant contexts. We introduce a simple, single-agent discovery harness built around LabBook, an agent-maintained memory that serves two complementary roles: guiding retrieval of relevant evidence from a complete experimental log and informing the generation of new solutions. At each iteration, the same agent combines its memory with retrieved evidence and jointly produces the next program and an updated LabBook. This separates complete history retention from selective context construction, without requiring an explicit population or branching search structure. translated_title: LabBook：利用实验历史实现高效的LLM驱动科学发现
translated_abstract: LLM驱动的科学发现中，进化方法通常从少量选定的祖先程序生成新程序。这种方式虽然使上下文保持可控，但可能遗漏其他实验中有用的证据；而包含完整的实验历史则会产生冗长且冗余的上下文。我们引入了一个简单的单智能体发现框架，该框架围绕LabBook构建——这是一种由智能体自身维护的记忆，发挥着两个互补的作用：指导从完整的实验日志中检索相关证据，并为新解决方案的生成提供参考信息。在每次迭代中，同一个智能体将其记忆与检索到的证据相结合，同时生成下一个程序并更新LabBook。这种设计将完整历史的保留与选择性的上下文构建分离开来，无需显式的种群或分支搜索结构。在49个Frontier-CS问题上，LabBook相比所评估的进化基线方法改善了观察到的质量-成本权衡。
tldr: LabBook是一种由智能体维护的记忆机制，通过将完整实验历史的保留与选择性上下文构建分离，使单智能体LLM发现框架在质量-成本权衡上超越了进化基线方法。
en_tdlr: LabBook is an agent-maintained memory that separates complete history retention from selective context construction, enabling a single-agent LLM discovery harness to achieve a better quality-cost trade-off than evolutionary baselines.
